skill.name: air-cryptographer

content.value_statement: AIR designs can hide subtle soundness gaps in selectors, boundaries, and global arguments. This skill gives a structured cryptographic review process for finding and explaining those risks.
actual_capabilities: Explains AIR design principles for STARK and zero-knowledge proof systems.
Reviews trace columns, row semantics, selectors, and boundary constraints.
Checks transition constraints, lookup arguments, permutation arguments, and memory consistency.
Identifies soundness risks such as unconstrained columns, selector leakage, and last-row escapes.
Produces review deliverables including constraint maps, degree tables, adversarial tests, and risk rankings.
limitations: Does not automatically verify code or run formal proof tools.
Requires the user to provide AIR definitions, constraints, or trace descriptions.
Focuses on soundness review, not production performance benchmarking.
May need extra context for custom fields, arithmetization choices, or protocol variants.

use_cases.title: Audit a New AIR Design
use_cases.description: Review a proposed trace layout and constraint set before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Soundness Review
use_cases.description: Turn a client specification into a checklist of risks, tests, and missing constraints.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Cryptographic Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare columns, degree growth, lookup usage, and transcript binding choices.

prompt_templates.title: Explain My AIR
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this AIR design in plain language. Identify the trace columns, row meaning, public inputs, and main constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Review Selector Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these selectors and gated constraints. Check booleanity, exclusivity, coverage, and whether any row can bypass enforcement.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Audit Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AIR soundness checklist for this specification. Include boundary, transition, lookup, permutation, memory, and transcript checks.

prompt_templates.title: Find Counterexample Traces
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as a cryptographic reviewer. Try to construct cheating traces that satisfy these constraints but violate the claimed statement.

output_examples.input: Review selector discipline for a CPU AIR with opcode flags and padding rows.
output_examples.output: The review flags selector coverage as the main risk. It recommends proving every selector is boolean, exactly one opcode is active, and padding cannot mimic execution rows.

output_examples.input: Assess a memory consistency argument that sorts by address and timestamp.
output_examples.output: The review checks whether reads link to prior writes, timestamps are monotonic, and the sorted log is tied back to the CPU trace.

output_examples.input: Prepare deliverables for a STARK AIR audit.
output_examples.output: The deliverables include a column inventory, constraint map, degree budget, adversarial witness tests, ranked findings, and concrete constraint fixes.

best_practices: Provide the trace layout, constraint definitions, boundary rules, and public input binding details together.
Ask for adversarial examples, not only descriptive feedback.
Review degree accounting and transcript binding before optimizing columns or lookups.
anti_patterns: Do not treat documented column meaning as proof that the column is constrained.
Do not gate constraints with selectors that are not themselves fully constrained.
Do not reuse challenges across arguments without checking algebraic cancellation risks.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps review AIR constraint systems used in STARK and zero-knowledge proof protocols.

faq.question: Can it prove my AIR is secure?
faq.answer: No. It supports expert review and counterexample search, but it is not a formal verification tool.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide trace columns, row semantics, constraints, boundary rules, public inputs, and any lookup or permutation arguments.

faq.question: Does it cover Fiat-Shamir issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks whether commitments, public inputs, trace length, and prover messages are bound before challenges.

faq.question: Can it help with performance choices?
faq.answer: Yes. It can discuss column count, degree growth, auxiliary columns, and local versus global argument tradeoffs.

faq.question: Is it limited to one proof system?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on AIR concepts that apply across STARK-style systems and related zero-knowledge designs.
